value.reason: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0% tax. A known customer with a region missing from rates.csv raises KeyError (team standard), not 0%.

value: pricing.unit_price(sku) -> Decimal (Decimal("0") if unknown); pricing.is_known_sku(sku) -> bool; pricing.customer_name(cid) -> str ("" if unknown); pricing.customer_discount(cid) -> Decimal multiplier (0.90 for 10% off; Decimal("1") for no discount or unknown customer)
why: Team standard: lookups return a default when nothing is found, but unit price 0 is a valid price, so an explicit is_known_sku() is needed to print UNKNOWN SKU lines. Discount is a multiplier per the standard, so its no-discount default is 1, not 0 (a deviation from the literal default-0 rule, flagged for acceptance).

value: tax.tax_for(customer_id, lines, discount_multiplier) -> (tax_amount Decimal rounded half-up to cent, tax_multiplier Decimal e.g. Decimal("1.0825") for 8.25%, Decimal("1") for 0% or unknown customer). lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for known skus only; discount_multiplier = customer discount multiplier from pricing. tax.py alone decides taxable base and rules; invoice.py only derives the displayed percent from tax_multiplier.
why: Tax rules live only in tax.py, which has the data. Passing lines and the discount multiplier lets tax.py decide taxability and the tax base. Displayed percent is derived from the multiplier, keeping the coding standard (8.25% = 1.0825).
